about: The lessons a new Prism library starts with (WO-41). Made once, by hand, from the shortlist in docs/industry-survey.md, section 3: the resource's title and link, where the survey found it (list:line), one line saying what it suggests for any project, and tags from prism_tags.json. Pointers into Grove's own requirements and work orders are left out. Rows of the shortlist whose link is not https are left out, as a refresh would leave them out. Loaded only into an empty library; a lesson's text is never edited in place afterwards.
source: docs/industry-survey.md, section 3 (sindresorhus/awesome at bc98e51 and the lists it points to)

lessons.title: Model Context Protocol
lessons.summary: Name the protocol revisions the server is verified against, and check them again on every SDK upgrade.

lessons.title: mcp
lessons.summary: Keep to the official SDK, pinned to one exact version, and add a transport only when a client needs it.

lessons.title: Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents
lessons.summary: Bound every tool result by default and give a visible way to get more: an agent's context is a budget.

lessons.title: context-tax
lessons.summary: Measure what the tool descriptions cost on every turn, and hold them to a byte budget with a test.

lessons.title: MCP Probe Kit
lessons.summary: List the tools over real stdio in a test and compare their names and input schemas with a stored snapshot.

lessons.title: Writing a Good CLAUDE.md
lessons.summary: Audit each line of the agent instruction file (would the agent err without it?) and keep detail in linked documents.

lessons.title: Claude Code Best Practices
lessons.summary: Base the conventions of an agent instruction file on the vendor's published guidance, and cite it.

lessons.title: Ctxlint
lessons.summary: Test that every command quoted in an agent instruction file still exists, by parsing it with the real argument parser.

lessons.title: LintLang
lessons.summary: Treat tool descriptions and agent instructions as tested artefacts: a check fails when one drifts from the code.

lessons.title: agnix
lessons.summary: Lint agent instruction files and MCP configuration as a development-only check.

lessons.title: agents-md-cookbook
lessons.summary: When several agent clients work on one repository, keep one canonical instruction source and point the other files to it.

lessons.title: Pluribus
lessons.summary: One canonical source, many instruction files: generate them or link them, never maintain copies.

lessons.title: Command Line Interface Guidelines
lessons.summary: Machine-readable output on stdout, messages on stderr, a zero or non-zero exit code; accept - for standard input where a file is expected; change the interface only by adding.

lessons.title: JSON Schema
lessons.summary: Publish a schema for each machine-readable result and validate real results against it in tests.

lessons.title: JSON-RPC
lessons.summary: Keep the application's own error codes clearly apart from protocol-level errors.

lessons.title: JSEND
lessons.summary: Use one envelope for success and for failure on every command, and freeze its shape.

lessons.title: SemVer Spec
lessons.summary: Write down what the public interface is, so that a version number means something.

lessons.title: jq
lessons.summary: Test that stdout is exactly one JSON document on success and on error, and document jq recipes for it.

lessons.title: RFC-3339 vs ISO-8601
lessons.summary: Name one timestamp format (RFC 3339, in UTC) and use it everywhere.

lessons.title: tldr
lessons.summary: Give example-first help: one worked example per command.

lessons.title: Architectural Decision Records
lessons.summary: Record each decision with its context and consequences, in a numbered log where a decision is superseded, never edited.

lessons.title: ARCHITECTURE.md
lessons.summary: Keep an architecture file with a map of the source code, the invariants and the design decisions.

lessons.title: The C4 Model
lessons.summary: Describe an architecture in levels (context, containers, components, code), so that each picture has one audience.

lessons.title: arc42
lessons.summary: Use a fixed section template for architecture documents, so that nothing is forgotten and a reader knows where to look.

lessons.title: What nobody tells you about documentation
lessons.summary: Give each document one role: tutorial, how-to guide, explanation or reference.

lessons.title: poliastro
lessons.summary: A worked example of documentation arranged by the four-part model: tutorials, how-to guides, explanation, reference.

lessons.title: sphinx-needs
lessons.summary: Model requirements as typed items with stable ids and links to the tests that cover them.

lessons.title: Living Documentation by Design, with Domain-Driven Design
lessons.summary: Check documentation against the code instead of trusting it, and treat drift as a defect.

lessons.title: Specification by Example
lessons.summary: Link requirement, example and test explicitly, for instance with a requirement id in the test name.

lessons.title: Mycelium
lessons.summary: Give every requirement or work order the same few fixed fields (goal, rationale, acceptance) and keep a decision log beside them.

lessons.title: CommonMark
lessons.summary: When code reads Markdown, name the specification and list which constructs are read and which are not.

lessons.title: GitHub Flavored Markdown Specifications
lessons.summary: Tables and task lists come from GitHub Flavored Markdown: say whether a Markdown reader supports that dialect.

lessons.title: markdown-it-py
lessons.summary: Use a real CommonMark parser as a development-only oracle for differential tests of hand-written Markdown patterns.

lessons.title: BlockWatch
lessons.summary: Tie documentation to code with a check that fails when one changes without the other.

lessons.title: Conventional Commits
lessons.summary: Adopt machine-readable commit types only when something consumes them, such as a changelog or a release tool.

lessons.title: There Are No Bugs, Just TODOs
lessons.summary: A tracker must show ownership, queue position, state, breakdown and closing; priority and severity fields add little.

lessons.title: How to do a code review
lessons.summary: Agree on a short, fixed list of what a reviewer checks, and record the review before work leaves review.

lessons.title: Feedback Ladders: How We Encode Code Reviews at Netlify
lessons.summary: Use a small closed vocabulary for how binding a review comment is.

lessons.title: Ship Small Diffs
lessons.summary: Keep each change small enough to review in one sitting: one work item per reviewable change.

lessons.title: presence
lessons.summary: Do not call work done without recorded evidence that its tests ran.

lessons.title: isitdone
lessons.summary: Done means the project's real checks passed on the exact tree that is delivered.

lessons.title: Concord MCP
lessons.summary: When several agents share a work list, make it visible who owns an item that is in progress.

lessons.title: Cookie licking
lessons.summary: Show the age of claimed, unfinished work so that abandoned claims are noticed; never release a claim automatically.

lessons.title: Blameless PostMortems and a Just Culture
lessons.summary: Write a short blameless note when a gate fails late or an assumption proves wrong, and keep it where the next person looks.

lessons.title: A collection of postmortem templates
lessons.summary: Pick one minimal postmortem template and use it for every incident note.

lessons.title: hypothesis
lessons.summary: Property-test parsers, tokenisers and query builders: any input, no exception, the same output twice.

lessons.title: coverage
lessons.summary: Measure coverage to find untested code, and be wary of a number gate: it invites tests written for the number.

lessons.title: Bats
lessons.summary: Test the shell scripts that guard a push or a release: a planted failure must fail and a clean tree must pass.

lessons.title: Naughty Strings
lessons.summary: Push a set of awkward strings through every place that takes text: keys, titles, bodies, queries, file names.

lessons.title: test-inventory
lessons.summary: Keep an inventory of skipped and expected-to-fail tests, with the reason for each.

lessons.title: VeriSpec
lessons.summary: Trace each statement of a specification to the test that proves it.

lessons.title: behave
lessons.summary: Golden-test the command line: replay recorded cases and compare the output.

lessons.title: The Fuzzing Book
lessons.summary: Fuzz every parser that takes untrusted input.

lessons.title: SlowFuzz: Automated Domain-Independent Detection of Algorithmic Complexity Vulnerabilities, 2017
lessons.summary: Test for algorithmic slowness as well as for crashes: worst-case input at the size cap must stay inside a time bound.

lessons.title: RegreSQL
lessons.summary: Keep golden results for important queries, so that a change in results or ranking shows up in review.

lessons.title: bats
lessons.summary: Shell-script tests with TAP output: a plain result format that other tools can read.

lessons.title: Runaway Regular Expressions: Catastrophic Backtracking
lessons.summary: Review every regular expression that meets untrusted text for superlinear backtracking, and cap the length of its input.

lessons.title: Python: re
lessons.summary: Possessive quantifiers and atomic groups in current Python remove some backtracking without a dependency.

lessons.title: recheck
lessons.summary: Run a checker for catastrophic backtracking over JavaScript-flavoured patterns; for other flavours read its findings as advice.

lessons.title: RE2
lessons.summary: Where untrusted input meets many patterns, weigh a non-backtracking engine; where a compiled dependency is unwelcome, bound the input instead.

lessons.title: ID_START / ID_CONTINUE
lessons.summary: Identifiers go beyond ASCII: say whether a tokeniser is ASCII-only, and what it skips.

lessons.title: Myths about File Paths
lessons.summary: Write down the path rules: how equality is decided, what happens with names that are not UTF-8, and what must stay inside which directory.

lessons.title: Falsehoods about text
lessons.summary: Check excerpting and key handling against the known falsehoods about text: length, case, characters and bytes.

lessons.title: Truths programmers should know about case
lessons.summary: Compare without case by case folding, not by lower-casing.

lessons.title: Don't you (forget NLP): Prompt injection with control characters in ChatGPT
lessons.summary: State a policy for control characters in text that is passed on to a model: they can carry an injection.

lessons.title: Trojan Source
lessons.summary: Bidirectional and format characters hide meaning from a reviewer: refuse them in source code and make them visible in text that is displayed.

lessons.title: CVE-2024-26150 Security Notice
lessons.summary: Treat every path argument that arrives from a template or an agent as untrusted: resolve it and check that it stays where it may be.

lessons.title: Falsehoods about Search
lessons.summary: Review search against a checklist: what stemming does to identifiers, and what an empty result means.

lessons.title: sqlite3
lessons.summary: Say clearly when the linked SQLite lacks a feature that is needed (FTS5, JSON), instead of failing with a general error.

lessons.title: Sqitch
lessons.summary: Pair every schema change with a verify step: a test per migration that upgrades from the previous version.

lessons.title: Atlas
lessons.summary: Test that a database migrated step by step equals one created fresh.

lessons.title: tbls
lessons.summary: Keep a data dictionary, and a check that it matches the real schema.

lessons.title: sqlite-utils
lessons.summary: Inspect a copy or a temporary database with maintenance tools, never the live file.

lessons.title: Litestream
lessons.summary: State a backup procedure for a SQLite file in WAL mode: copying the main file alone is not one.

lessons.title: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 (2026)
lessons.summary: Name the OWASP GenAI risks in the threat model of anything that feeds text to a model.

lessons.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
lessons.summary: Content that an assistant retrieves can carry planted instructions: treat retrieved text as data.

lessons.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Through MCP Tools: A Defense Guide
lessons.summary: Classify each tool by whether its result can carry text written outside the trust boundary, and tell the client.

lessons.title: Why content-based prompt-injection detection has a structural blind spot
lessons.summary: A marker inside the text that says 'this is data' can be forged by the text: mark provenance in a separate field that the server sets.

lessons.title: Agents Rule of Two: A Practical Approach to AI Agent Security
lessons.summary: A component that supplies untrusted input to an agent must not also give it outbound actions.

lessons.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
lessons.summary: Keep result shapes friendly to a client that isolates untrusted content.

lessons.title: Anyone can Access Deleted and Private Repository Data on GitHub
lessons.summary: Anything pushed to a public repository is exposed for good: check every commit of a push, not only the newest.

lessons.title: Hidden GitHub Commits and How to Reveal Them
lessons.summary: Write down what to do when a secret was pushed: rotate it first, because removing the commit does not unpublish it.

lessons.title: Git hooks documentation at git-scm.com
lessons.summary: A pre-push hook is given the remote's commit for each ref: use it to check the whole range that is pushed.

lessons.title: Gitleaks
lessons.summary: Run a maintained secret scanner in development or CI, as a second line behind your own patterns.

lessons.title: Proactive Controls
lessons.summary: Walk the ten OWASP proactive controls once and record which of them apply.

lessons.title: Python chapter of Fedora Defensive Coding Guide
lessons.summary: Review the code once against a short, Python-specific list of things to avoid.

lessons.title: Bandit
lessons.summary: Run the Python security linter and read each report: SQL text built with f-strings deserves a look every time.

lessons.title: pip-audit
lessons.summary: Audit pinned dependencies against known vulnerabilities on a schedule: with exact pins nothing updates by itself.

lessons.title: Statement on event-stream compromise" (under @dominictarr, scuttlebot and others)
lessons.summary: Keep dependencies few, and write down how an update is reviewed before it is taken.

lessons.title: Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure Part 1: Preventing pwn requests
lessons.summary: In a public repository, test pull requests with the pull_request event only.

lessons.title: Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure Part 2: Untrusted input
lessons.summary: Never interpolate pull-request titles, branch names or other untrusted values into workflow scripts.

lessons.title: PPE — Poisoned Pipeline Execution
lessons.summary: A job that runs code from a pull request must hold no secrets and a read-only token.

lessons.title: The GitHub Actions Worm: Compromising GitHub Repositories Through the Actions Dependency Tree
lessons.summary: Pin every CI action to a full commit SHA.

lessons.title: zizmor
lessons.summary: Lint workflow files for security mistakes from the first workflow commit.

lessons.title: actionlint
lessons.summary: Lint workflow files for mistakes in syntax and expressions.

lessons.title: ruff
lessons.summary: One fast tool for linting as a development-only gate: start with the rules that find mistakes, and weigh reformatting separately.

lessons.title: mypy
lessons.summary: Run a type checker and read its reports before deciding whether it becomes a gate.

lessons.title: PEP-586
lessons.summary: Type closed sets of values (a status, a kind, an error code) as literals.

lessons.title: PEP-589
lessons.summary: Type dictionary shapes that cross a boundary (envelopes, rows) with TypedDict: it costs nothing at run time.

lessons.title: import-linter
lessons.summary: Enforce import rules between modules, so that layering is checked and not only described.

lessons.title: shellcheck
lessons.summary: Lint every shell script in the repository.

lessons.title: shfmt
lessons.summary: A formatter for shell scripts earns its place once there are more than a few of them.

lessons.title: Greg Wooledge's (aka "greycat") wiki
lessons.summary: Review scripts that loop over file names or commit ranges against the well-known pitfalls.

lessons.title: codespell
lessons.summary: Check spelling in documentation and identifiers: a misspelt word hides text from search.

lessons.title: actions/checkout
lessons.summary: Use the first-party checkout action, pinned by its full commit SHA.

lessons.title: pre-commit
lessons.summary: A hook framework earns its place with many hooks; one script and core.hooksPath need none.

lessons.title: uv
lessons.summary: Run gates against the frozen lock file, so that a gate never resolves new versions.

lessons.title: LWC
lessons.summary: For a memory tool that agents use: bounded recall, citations, atomic writes and a read-only server mode.

lessons.title: LLMSlim
lessons.summary: Let a caller state a size budget on get and on search, and report what was cut.

lessons.title: Selvedge
lessons.summary: Record why a change was made, by linking a note to the work item or the commit.

lessons.title: fable
lessons.summary: Make 'what is read back is byte for byte what was written' a tested property of stored notes.

lessons.title: PLUR
lessons.summary: Keep an agent's memory in plain text that a person can read and correct.

lessons.title: Librarian
lessons.summary: Offer matching on part of an identifier in a search over notes.

lessons.title: IssueDB
lessons.summary: A command-line issue tracker built for agents: compare command surfaces before designing your own.

lessons.title: gemini-beads
lessons.summary: Task memory can live in git instead of a database: weigh it as a storage choice.

lessons.title: Repowise
lessons.summary: Deterministic, model-free scores per file are possible: decide whether a score helps, or only ranks.
